the tickerplant is the spawned PEER and di.subscriptions runs here, not the other way round: a q
process blocked in a sync call does not accept a new inbound connection (measured - the subscriber
dialling back into a busy parent times out), so the side that DIALS has to be the side that drives.
that is also how di/rdb and di/subscriptions arrange their own suites.

VERSION guards. these are LOAD-time, so they can only be observed in a CHILD process - the module
is already loaded here and cannot be reloaded with a different VERSION file. a temp QPATH tree
symlinks every other module and copies di/tickerplant so only its VERSION is altered

comment: load di.tickerplant in a child q against that tree. QPATH MUST be set for the child - inheriting ours makes it load the REAL module and every case passes vacuously
control: an untouched VERSION must load cleanly
a missing VERSION must fail loudly and name the module
an empty VERSION must fail loudly and name the module
a padded VERSION must load and be TRIMMED. written from q, not shell printf - the quoting does not survive system[] and silently produces an empty file, which tests the wrong guard
remove the VERSION-guard trees

control - a clean VERSION loads and reports the exact version. BRACKETED because writing a bare string through 0:/read0 strips trailing spaces, which would destroy the padding the last assert looks for

code: 0<count VMISSING ss "di.tickerplant: VERSION file missing or unreadable"
comment: a missing VERSION names di.tickerplant rather than surfacing a raw OS error that points nowhere

code: 0<count VEMPTY ss "di.tickerplant: VERSION file is empty"
comment: an empty VERSION is rejected, not accepted as a version that reads to di.depcheck as 'exports no version'
a padded VERSION is TRIMMED to the bare semver. asserts the VALUE, not just that it loaded - the naive read loads happily and hands di.depcheck a padded string di.depcheck compares as a string
